memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: God called the light "day," and the darkness he called "night." And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day. - Gen 1:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives names to what He has made. He calls the light "day" and the darkness "night." In naming them, God shows His authority over creation. To name something, in the thinking of the Bible, is to have rightful ownership and care over it. The day and the night both belong to God, and both answer to Him.

Notice too the rhythm God sets: "there was evening, and there was morning." God builds a pattern of time into the world, seasons of light and darkness, work and rest, activity and stillness. Life is not meant to be all daylight with no night, nor all night with no dawn. God orders our days with both.

This is a quiet comfort. If you are in a dark season right now, remember that God rules the night just as surely as the day. He has not lost control when the light fades. Morning always follows evening in His good design, and He is the One who brings the dawn.

Every new day is a fresh gift from His hand (Lam 3:22-23). And there is a greater morning coming for all who belong to Christ, a day with no more night at all (Rev 21:25). Until then, trust the God who holds both your days and your nights.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you in a "day" or a "night" season right now, and where is God in it?
2. How can you thank God for both the rest of evening and the fresh start of morning?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You rule over my days and my nights. Help me trust You in the dark seasons and welcome each new morning as a gift from You. Amen.
